question: After fixing the infrastructure bug (SameFileError in run_experiment_distributed.py line 368 where src and dst both resolve to the same testbed_server.py) AND fixing C1 behavioral detection control to exclude 304 responses (consistent with parent metric's 304 exclusion), does C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 achieve CONFIRMED status on distributed infrastructure with n_non304>=800?
hypothesis: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 will be CONFIRMED on distributed multi-node infrastructure after fixing two bugs: (1) SameFileError by removing unnecessary file copy and using parent testbed_server.py directly; (2) C1 behavioral detection control excluding 304 responses from TP/TN calculation. The parent MEASUREMENT_INVALID outcome was an infrastructure crash (SameFileError), not evidence against orthogonality. The grandparent's primary orthogonality metric independently confirms orthogonality (r=-0.0585, CI upper 0.0163 < 0.15, n_non304=688, audit PASS). Excluding 304s from C1 yields mean TN=1.0 (audit-confirmed). With n_non304>=800 target, all C1-C7 conditions are expected to pass.
falsifier: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality is REJECTED at delta=0.15 if ANY of the following occurs after the two fixes: (C1) behavioral detection mean TP < 0.85 OR mean TN < 0.85 on distributed infrastructure (after 304 exclusion); (C2) fewer than 2/3 endpoints have non-304 behavioral signal std > 0 OR fewer than 2/3 have non-304 structural signal std > 0; (C3) 95% CI upper bound of endpoint-stratified pooled Pearson r (non-304 only) >= 0.15 on distributed testbed; (C4) TOST equivalence test p_upper >= 0.05 at delta=0.15 (one-sided, non-304 only); (C5) endpoint-stratified cache-mode heterogeneity: |r_stratified_enabled - r_stratified_disabled| >= 2 * SE_pooled; (C6) B-LOCAL-ONLY baseline shows |r| >= 0.15 (regression from LOCAL parent); (C7) B-CONFOUND-DISTRIBUTED shows endpoint-stratified weighted |r| < 0.15 (confound fails to reproduce). C-FRESHNESS orthogonality is MEASUREMENT_INVALID if infrastructure failure prevents data collection or if n_non304 < 400.

baselines.description: Single-node Flask testbed WITHOUT concurrent load or multi-node distribution — identical to parent EXP-GRAPH-35530590140 LOCAL testbed. Regression-free baseline confirmation.

Multi-node distributed testbed: 2 independent Flask processes on separate ports (18971, 18972), each with independent SQLite database and in-memory CDN cache. Round-robin request routing. Each node independently generates ETag/Cache-Control headers. Cache invalidation on one node does NOT propagate to the other.

Single-node Flask testbed with 5 concurrent client sessions making simultaneous requests. Tests whether request contention, timing jitter, and interleaved cache states introduce behavioral-structural coupling.

Distributed negative control: same multi-node architecture as B-DISTRIBUTED but with V2 confound (fixed 'expired' request_id for expired responses, uuid4 for valid). Expected to reproduce the confound (|r| >= 0.15) across distributed nodes.
baselines.expected: |r| >= 0.15 (negative control confirming confound is genuine in distributed setting)

positive_control: Token validation failure detection on distributed infrastructure: behavioral signal must correctly identify expired vs valid tokens with TP >= 0.85 across all distributed nodes. After 304 exclusion from C1, all cache-enabled valid-token conditions that previously produced TN=0.0588 (due to 304 being treated as behavioral change) will now correctly exclude 304 responses, yielding TN=1.0 for those conditions.
null_control: Structural signal std > 0 across all non-304 conditions on distributed infrastructure: independent ETag generation per node, Cache-Control headers, and UUID-based dynamic content should produce non-zero structural variation even on cache-disabled responses. Behavioral std should be non-zero on conditions with auth state variation.
measurement_validity: SAMEFILEERROR FIX: Remove unnecessary shutil.copy2 block (lines 364-368) that copies testbed_server.py from parent experiment dir. The copy was for provenance only — the experiment already uses parent_dir/testbed_server.py directly as the server script. Provenance is recorded via SHA-256 hash of the parent's files. This eliminates the SameFileError that crashed the parent.

C1 304-EXCLUSION FIX: C1 behavioral detection control now excludes 304 responses from TP/TN calculation. 304 cache-hit responses are HTTP caching artifacts, not behavioral signal changes. This is consistent with the primary orthogonality metric which already excludes 304s. The fix filters 304 rows before computing C1 TP/TN in compute_c1().
V_ETAG_PERMISSION_LEAKAGE FIX (inherited from grandparent): testbed_server.py decodes expired JWT tokens WITHOUT verification to extract permission_level for ETag generation.
V3 ENDPOINT-STRATIFICATION (inherited from grandparent): Pooled Pearson r uses endpoint-stratified weighting, not simple concatenation.
V1 UUID FOR ALL STATUS CODES (inherited from grandparent): All request_ids use uuid.uuid4() for all status codes in primary testbed.
304 EXCLUSION: 304 responses excluded from pooled correlation, per-endpoint correlations, per-cache correlations, AND C1 behavioral detection control.
DISTRIBUTED INDEPENDENCE: Each Flask node has independent SQLite database, independent in-memory cache, independent ETag generation. No shared state between nodes.
CACHE INDEPENDENCE: Cache invalidation on node A does NOT propagate to node B. Each node CDN simulation operates independently.
ROUND-ROBIN ROUTING: Distributed testbed routes requests round-robin across nodes. Each node receives approximately equal load.
NON-304 POWER: n >= 800 non-304 samples (target: 42 per condition per endpoint x 8 conditions x 3 endpoints = 1012 total, ~850 non-304 at 84% rate).
TOST ONE-SIDED: C3 tests CI upper < 0.15 only; C4 tests TOST p_upper < 0.05 only (one-sided).

Structural signal extraction uses ONLY: (a) ETag change (0/1), (b) Cache-Control change (0/1), (c) normalized Shannon entropy of UUID-based request_id, (d) SHA256(request_id)[:16] as int % 10000 / 10000.
Each endpoint has independent behavioral and structural signal extraction — no shared variables between signal domains.
decision_rule: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality at delta=0.15 on distributed infrastructure is CONFIRMED if ALL of: (C1) behavioral detection mean TP >= 0.85 AND mean TN >= 0.85 across all endpoints on distributed testbed (AFTER 304 EXCLUSION); (C2) at least 2/3 endpoints have non-304 behavioral signal std > 0 AND at least 2/3 have non-304 structural signal std > 0; (C3) 95% CI upper bound of endpoint-stratified pooled Pearson r (non-304 samples only) < 0.15 on distributed testbed; (C4) TOST equivalence test p_upper < 0.05 at delta=0.15 (one-sided, non-304 samples only); (C5) endpoint-stratified cache-mode heterogeneity check (non-304 samples): |r_stratified_enabled - r_stratified_disabled| < 2 * SE_pooled; (C6) B-LOCAL-ONLY baseline shows |r| < 0.15 (no regression from parent); (C7) B-CONFOUND-DISTRIBUTED shows endpoint-stratified weighted |r| >= 0.15 (negative control passes). C-FRESHNESS orthogonality is REJECTED if ANY condition fails. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if infrastructure failure prevents data collection or n_non304 < 400.
product_consequence_positive: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality confirmed on distributed production-like infrastructure with n_non304>=800. Parallel-channel architecture (separate behavioral and structural signal processing) is justified for multi-node deployment. Product may proceed with dual-signal freshness detection across distributed cache topologies. The two bugs are confirmed resolved.
product_consequence_negative: C-FRESHNESS orthogonality fails on distributed infrastructure even with both fixes. Parallel-channel architecture is NOT justified for multi-node deployment. Product must investigate cache-coupling as a correlation source and potentially use fused classifiers. Identifies a genuine distributed infrastructure barrier beyond the measurement artifacts.
estimated_cost: Low: (1) Fix SameFileError — remove ~5 line copy block, record parent file hashes for provenance; (2) C1 304-exclusion fix already in parent code; (3) Execute 4 conditions (B-LOCAL-ONLY, B-DISTRIBUTED, B-CONCURRENT, B-CONFOUND-DISTRIBUTED) ~3-4 hours with 42 samples/condition/endpoint; (4) Analysis ~30 min. Total: 4-5 compute-hours. Infrastructure reused from parent.
expected_information_gain: Very high: this is the minimum cost experiment that resolves the primary unknown from parent EXP-GRAPH-35544808911 — whether C-FRESHNESS orthogonality achieves CONFIRMED status on distributed infrastructure. The two fixes are targeted code changes that directly address the sole reasons for the parent's MEASUREMENT_INVALID outcome. The grandparent's primary orthogonality metric already passes independently. A positive result (CONFIRMED) changes a product decision: parallel-channel architecture justified for multi-node deployment. A negative result (any C1-C7 fails after fixes) identifies a genuine distributed infrastructure barrier. Either outcome is high-information for C-FRESHNESS claim advancement.
